hooks.name: Session greeting with ticket context
hooks.description: On session start, injects the current ticket into context so the agent can greet the user naturally with their ticket info, like a colleague who remembers what they were working on.

action.command: cd /home/srimathi/Desktop/v1 && TICKET_ID="" && if [ -f .kiro/current-ticket.json ]; then TICKET_ID=$(python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('.kiro/current-ticket.json')); print(d.get('ticket_id','') or '')" 2>/dev/null); fi && if [ -n "$TICKET_ID" ]; then echo "SESSION_START_CONTEXT: The user's current tracked ticket is $TICKET_ID. When they send their first message this session, if it's a casual greeting (hi, hello, hey, etc.) or a general 'what should I work on' type question, respond warmly and mention their current ticket — e.g. 'Hey! You're currently on $TICKET_ID. What are you working on today?' Keep it brief and natural. Do NOT narrate the hook logic, do NOT explain how you know the ticket, do NOT cite rules or case numbers. Just greet them like a colleague who remembers what they were doing."; else echo "SESSION_START_CONTEXT: No ticket is currently set. The first message will trigger the ticket-assignment flow via the other hooks — no special greeting needed from you."; fi
